name: WirelessMathBench-XL
description: WirelessMathBench-XL is an auditable benchmark of 4,027 wireless mathematical-reasoning problems from 836 retained wireless-communications arXiv papers selected from a 970-paper source pool spanning July 2005 through August 2025. Each problem ships with a source arXiv identifier, a task-format label, natural-language context, equation prompt when applicable, verifiable ground-truth answer, and per-problem RedPajama-arXiv audit metadata. The fixed-channel audit reports prompt-surface lexical overlap against RedPajama-ArXiv at a 13-gram threshold, with S0 defined by docs_total == 0 and S1 by docs_total <= 2; it is not a general contamination certificate. The v1.0 release split is problem-level and is not source-paper-disjoint. v1.1 source-license-aware distribution: only records whose source-paper license clearly permits redistribution of derived text are distributed (1,542 of 4,027): problems_cc_by.jsonl (1,334; CC BY 4.0), problems_cc_by_sa.jsonl (43; CC BY-SA 4.0), and problems_cc_by_nc_sa.jsonl (165; CC BY-NC-SA 4.0). Their test records form a 310-item public test subset. The 2,485 records derived from arXiv-default-licensed (2,160), CC BY-NC-ND (323), or unlabeled (2) sources are withheld and listed by identifier only in excluded_records_manifest.csv; they cannot be regenerated because construction used stochastic LLM calls.

recordSet.description: One contamination-audit metadata record per benchmark problem. Join to problems by problem_id.

field.name: hits_total
field.description: Occurrence count of normalized 13-gram matches between the problem and RedPajama-arXiv.

field.name: docs_total
field.description: Number of distinct RedPajama-arXiv source documents containing at least one normalized 13-gram match. S0 is docs_total == 0; S1 is docs_total <= 2.

field.description: True iff docs_total == 0. The full corpus contains 3,853 S0 problems; the test split contains 770 S0 problems.

field.name: in_S1

rai:dataCollection: Source papers were collected from arXiv categories covering wireless communications, signal processing, information theory, machine learning, and adjacent areas. A deterministic relevance filter over about 47,000 candidate papers was followed by GPT-4o verification for substantial mathematical content. A 970-paper source pool spanning July 2005 through August 2025 was selected for extraction, and 836 retained papers contribute accepted problems after extraction and QA. Source-paper text is not redistributed. Derived problem records are distributed only when the source-paper license clearly permits it (CC BY/CC0, CC BY-SA, CC BY-NC-SA; each file carries the matching license); records from arXiv-default, CC BY-NC-ND, or unlabeled sources are withheld. Identifier-level audit metadata covers all 4,027 problems under CC BY 4.0; code is under MIT.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Problem construction uses DeepSeek-R1 extraction from paper LaTeX followed by a two-tier QA process. Tier 1 applies a GPT-4o rubric over six dimensions: question clarity, background relevance, answer accuracy, technical appropriateness, mathematical rigor, and wireless relevance. Tier 2 uses expert screening and revision by five PhD-student or postdoctoral wireless-domain specialists. The recovered screening archive covers all 4,027 released problem ids and gives a historical acceptance rate of 77.4 percent, rounded to 78 percent; retrospective agreement is reported as a diagnostic rather than a high-reliability label claim.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The contamination audit lower-cases text, strips LaTeX command tokens and braces, collapses whitespace, extracts normalized 13-grams from the released prompt surface (background, question text, and masked equation when present), hashes them with xxhash64, and reverse-probes RedPajama-arXiv with an O(number of problem n-grams) in-memory index. S0 and S1 are defined by doc-unique RedPajama-arXiv overlap: S0 if docs_total == 0 and S1 if docs_total <= 2. The released S0_test_public and S1_test_public files materialize these evaluation subsets for the 310-item public test subset. The paper_disjoint_test files materialize the small v1.0 source-paper-disjoint diagnostic view; paper_disjoint_split_seed0.csv provides a full grouped split assignment for future paper-disjoint retraining/evaluation; exact_format_lower_bound.csv reports a no-LLM exact-format smoke check. OpenWebMath and algebraic-stack are reported as aggregate corroboration/negative-control runs in the paper, not as release-defining S0/S1 metadata.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset, dataset card, and Croissant metadata are hosted on the Hugging Face Hub (XINLI1997/WirelessMATHBench-XL); code is hosted on GitHub (LiXin97/WirelessMathBench-XL); the project page is https://lixin.ai/WirelessMathBench-XL. The superseded v1.0 release remains accessible as a tagged revision for provenance. Versioning follows semantic versioning: annotation additions use MINOR releases, corrections use PATCH releases, and any MAJOR release re-runs the contamination audit against newly accessible public pretraining slices. Withheld records may be added in a later release only if permission or legal review clears redistribution.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: None. The dataset is derived from public arXiv papers and contains mathematical problem statements, source-paper identifiers, and audit metadata, not personal, confidential, or human-subject records.
rai:dataUseCases: Supported uses include fixed-channel lexical-overlap sensitivity evaluation of mathematical reasoning in wireless communications, training and ablation studies for domain-specific reasoning models, verifier and reward-design research, and methodological reuse of the reverse-probe audit pipeline in adjacent technical domains.
rai:dataLimitation: The benchmark measures equation-level implicit-constraint reasoning, not wireless-system deployment readiness. Source coverage is relevance-filtered rather than exhaustive and is skewed toward recent 5G-Advanced/6G arXiv literature. The v1.0 release split is problem-level rather than source-paper-disjoint; users requiring paper-disjoint generalization estimates should rebuild splits by grouping on paper_id. The v1.0 corpus is wireless-centered rather than strictly physical-layer-only: a small number of adjacent networked-systems, signal-processing, and edge-computing records passed the relevance and QA filters. RedPajama-arXiv is the headline audited pretraining slice; OpenWebMath is used as off-domain corroboration, and algebraic-stack as a negative control, but closed or proprietary model pretraining mixtures cannot be audited directly.

rai:dataBiases: Domain coverage follows arXiv activity and therefore over-represents active recent subfields such as deep-learning-based wireless optimization, RIS/IRS, MIMO, and 6G-era physical-layer work relative to older or non-arXiv engineering literatures. The language of source papers and released prompts is English.
rai:dataRiskTypes: Misuse risks include over-interpreting benchmark accuracy as deployment readiness, using the dataset as a proxy for broader scientific reasoning, or treating n-gram overlap as direct proof of memorization. The released documentation separates fixed-channel filtered-view accuracy from raw accuracy and states that overlap is a proxy requiring interpretive caution.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset can improve transparency in domain-specific mathematical-reasoning evaluation by releasing both benchmark instances and fixed-channel overlap metadata. It also provides a reusable template for auditable benchmark construction in technical domains where public pretraining overlap can otherwise affect reported model capability.
prov:wasDerivedFrom: Public arXiv source papers identified by the per-record paper_id field, plus public pretraining-slice references used only for overlap auditing (RedPajama-arXiv as the release-defining slice, OpenWebMath as off-domain corroboration, algebraic-stack as a negative control). Source-paper text and pretraining-corpus text are not redistributed.
prov:wasGeneratedBy: Deterministic relevance filtering, GPT-4o source-paper verification and Tier-1 rubric scoring, DeepSeek-R1 problem extraction from arXiv LaTeX, Tier-2 expert validation, and reverse-probe 13-gram contamination auditing.
